ja2en.まだ見ぬ結末について: About the endings you have not seen
ja2en.犯人を見つけたのに、まだ見ていない結末があるみたいなんです。: I found the culprit, and yet there still seems to be an ending I haven't seen.
ja2en.人の事件が片づいても、館まで素直に口を開くとは限らないよ。: Settling a case among people doesn't mean the house will open its mouth as readily.
ja2en.しかも黙秘が得意でね。事件の外に置かれたものを見直してごらん。: And it's very good at staying silent. Try looking again at what was left outside the case.
ja2en.別の結末を望むなら、最後の推理より、事件が起きる前の歩き方を疑うべきだ。: If you want a different ending, doubt not your final deduction but the way you walked before the murder.
ja2en.事件の前？ 結末を分けるのは、最後の推理じゃないんですか。: Before the murder? Isn't it the last deduction that decides the ending?
ja2en.夜に必要な問いは、明るいうちでなければ育たないものさ。: The questions you need at night can only be grown while it is still light.
ja2en.夜になってから帳尻を合わせようとしても遅い？: So it's too late to balance the books once night falls?
ja2en.館の時計は案外せっかちでね。日が落ちるころには、開かなくなる扉もある。: This house keeps an impatient clock. By sundown, some doors no longer open.
ja2en.『日暮れまでに全部集めろ』ではないんですね。: So it isn't “collect everything before dusk.”
ja2en.集めるのではなく、誰がなぜ来たのかを気にしておく。: Not collecting. Minding who came, and why.
ja2en.そして、この館が見せる形と、隠したがる形の違いを覚えておく。: And remembering the difference between the shape this house shows and the shape it would rather hide.
ja2en.人と建物、両方の事情を考える。: Think about the people and the building both.
ja2en.そう。事件の証拠だけを追うと、事件の外にある扉を見失う。: Just so. Chase only the evidence of the case, and you lose sight of the door outside it.
ja2en.苦い結末を見た後でも、やり直せますか？: Even after a bitter ending, can I start over?
ja2en.もちろん。結末は行き止まりではなく、次に見る場所を照らす街灯だよ。: Of course. An ending is not a dead end but a street lamp, lighting the next place to look.
ja2en.街灯にしては、だいぶ暗かったですけど。: For a street lamp, it was awfully dark.
ja2en.だから相談所を建てた。照明費は出ないがね。: Which is why I built this consultation room. Though nobody pays the lighting bill.
ja2en.真エンディングへのぶっちゃけ話: Straight talk about the true ending
ja2en.舞黒さん。今日は真エンディングへの行き方を、もう少しぶっちゃけてください。: Mr Maicro. Today I'd like you to be a little more blunt about how to reach the true ending.
ja2en.名前からして、ずいぶん答えに近い相談だね。: By the name of it, that's a request awfully close to the answer itself.
ja2en.答えそのものではなく、昼と夜に何を残せばいいかだけ。: Not the answer. Only what I should leave behind by day and by night.
ja2en.なら、昼は事件を追う時間ではない。館が隠している道具と入口を探す時間だ。: Then the daytime is not for chasing the case. It is for finding the tools and the entrances the house is hiding.
ja2en.談話室の古い声を聞き流さないこと。四つの数字は、もっと高い場所の陽だまりで役に立: Do not let the old voice in the drawing room wash over you. Four numbers will serve you in a sunnier place, higher up.
ja2en.数字で開くものの中に、館の形を知る手掛かりがある。: Inside whatever those numbers open, there's a clue to the shape of the house.
ja2en.もう一つ。館に散った三つの色は、重ねて初めて命令になる。読めたら、机は正面から眺: One more. The three colours scattered through the house become an order only when laid one over another. Once you can read it, throw away the notion that a desk is a thing you look at from the front.
ja2en.上、横、それでもなければ……裏側。: On top, at the side, and if not there... underneath.
ja2en.その二つを手にしたら、古い模型と今の部屋の奥行きを比べる。合わない場所には理由が: With those two in hand, compare the old model against the depth of the room as it stands. Where they disagree, there is a reason.
ja2en.見つけるだけじゃなく、夕食前に中まで入っておく。: Not just find it, but get inside before dinner.
ja2en.そう。それが昼の宿題だ。ついでに、遠くから来た客が何を探しているのか聞ければ申し: Just so. That is the day's homework. And if you can also ask what the guest from far away is looking for, so much the better.
ja2en.夜は毒だけを追わないこと。昼に転んだ執務室の椅子を、ただの思い出で終わらせない。: At night, do not chase only the poison. Do not let the study chair you fell from by day end as a mere memory.
ja2en.椅子の周りに、昔の人たちを結ぶ記録が残っている。: There's a record around that chair, tying the old ones together.
ja2en.そして一階の陽だまりへ戻る。Aなら床の痕跡、Bなら植物の足元を調べた、その先だ。: Then back to the sunlit room downstairs. On A, past where you examined the mark on the floor; on B, past the foot of the plant.
ja2en.毒の手掛かりを見つけて満足せず、床そのものをもう一度見る。: Don't stop at finding the trace of the poison. Look at the floor itself again.
ja2en.昼に地下書斎へ入っていれば、今度は別の入口が君に見つけられる。: And if you went into the underground study by day, this time another entrance will let you find it.
ja2en.昼に館の道具と隠し部屋。夜に古い記録ともう一つの地下。客の目的も忘れない。: By day: the tools and the hidden room. By night: the old records and the second basement. And don't forget the guest's purpose.
ja2en.そこまで揃えて事件を解けば、館のほうから続きを話し始めるよ。これ以上は本当に答え: Gather all of that and then solve the case, and the house itself will begin telling you the rest. Any further and I really would be giving you the answer.
ja2en.前と違うルートへ行きたいんです。: I'd like to go down a different route this time.
ja2en.システム上の話です。: I mean in the system sense.
ja2en.庭では、どこへ行ったかより、いつ遠回りしたかが後まで響く。: In the garden, it matters less where you went than when you took the long way round.
ja2en.分かれ道は、目の前に標識が出るとは限らない。: A fork does not always come with a signpost in front of it.
ja2en.午後の庭で、何を見てから散策へ向かったか。そこから考えるといい。: In the afternoon garden, what did you look at before you set off on the walk? Start from there.
ja2en.そう。君が動く時刻が変われば、他の人が館を出入りする時刻も変わる。: Just so. Change the hour at which you move, and the hours at which others come and go change with it.
ja2en.人の予定がずれると、事件の準備もずれる。: If people's schedules shift, so do the preparations for the murder.
ja2en.使える部屋、手に取れる道具、残る痕跡。どれも少しずつ変わる。: Which rooms are free, which tools can be picked up, which traces remain. All of it shifts a little.
ja2en.犯人が変わるわけではないんですよね。: But the culprit doesn't change, does he.
ja2en.役者は同じでも、舞台装置が違えば芝居は変わる。: The cast is the same, but change the set and the play changes.
ja2en.まず庭での自分の行動順を比べてみる。: First I'll compare the order I did things in the garden.
ja2en.同じ選択を繰り返すより、散策へ向かうまでの寄り道を変えてごらん。: Rather than repeat the same choice, try changing where you stop off on your way to the walk.
ja2en.一個ずつ試すしかないんですか？: Is there nothing for it but to try them one at a time?
ja2en.探偵は比較が仕事だよ。総当たりと言うと急に格好が悪くなるがね。: Comparison is a detective's trade. Though it sounds far less dashing when you call it brute force.
ja2en.言い換えても総当たりは総当たりです。: Rephrasing it doesn't stop it being brute force.
ja2en.最後の犯行を止めるには: How to stop the last murder
ja2en.あの場面、すぐ動いたら間に合わなかったんです。: In that scene, moving straight away meant I didn't get there in time.
ja2en.人を救おうとして、誰より早く動きたい時はある。: There are moments when, wanting to save someone, you want to move before anyone else.
ja2en.けれど、勇気と早撃ちは別物だよ。: But courage and a quick draw are two different things.
ja2en.早く選べばいいわけじゃない……？: So choosing fast isn't the point...?
ja2en.あの場面では、君の手より先に、全員の視線がどこへ向いているかを見る。: In that scene, before your own hands, watch where everyone's eyes are turned.
ja2en.助けたい人ではなく、見ている人？: Not the person I want to save, but the people watching?
ja2en.動けば止められるのか。動くことで、誰かの判断を早めてしまわないか。: Will moving stop it? Or will moving hurry someone else's decision?
ja2en.行動の速さではなく、きっかけの順番を考える。: Not the speed of the act, but the order of what sets it off.
ja2en.そう。何もしない時間にも、場面を変える働きがある。: Just so. Even time spent doing nothing does its work on a scene.
ja2en.待っているだけで状況が良くなるとは思えません。: I can't believe simply waiting makes things better.
ja2en.待つ目的は安全になることではない。視線と立ち位置が変わる瞬間を見つけることだ。: The point of waiting is not to be safe. It is to catch the moment when the eyes and the positions change.
ja2en.その瞬間が来たら、手元を見直す。: And when that moment comes, look again at what's in my hands.
ja2en.道具の名前に用途を決めさせないこと。探偵の持ち物は、説明書より融通が利く。: Don't let a tool's name decide its use. A detective's belongings are more flexible than their instructions.
ja2en.また行儀の悪い案を勧めていますね。: You're recommending badly behaved ideas again.
ja2en.まず、誰が誰を見ているか。次に、待つと何が変わるか。: First: who is watching whom. Then: what changes if I wait.
ja2en.そこまで考えれば、君自身の案が出るはずだ。: Think that far and your own idea should come to you.
ja2en.出なかったら、また相談に来ます。: And if it doesn't, I'll come and consult you again.
ja2en.夜の探索を有利に進めたい: Making the night search go better
ja2en.零度警部の信頼を得ると、捜査が有利になるんですか？: Does winning Inspector Reido's trust actually make the investigation easier?
ja2en.信頼は時間をくれるものではない。迷わない時間と交換するものだよ。: Trust does not give you time. You trade it for time not spent lost.
ja2en.得したのか損したのか、もう怪しいんですけど。: I'm already unsure whether that's a gain or a loss.
ja2en.信を得た探偵は少し遅れて歩き出す代わりに、警部の見立てをひとつ持っている。: A trusted detective sets off a little later, but carries one of the inspector's readings with her.
ja2en.道に迷えば、次に見るべき部屋も何度でも相談できる。: And if you lose your way, you can ask him which room to look at next, as often as you like.
ja2en.信頼されなかった場合は？: And if he doesn't trust me?
ja2en.早く放り出される。ただし居間は、しばらく警察のものだ。: You are thrown out sooner. Though the living room belongs to the police for a while.
ja2en.純粋な上位互換ではないんですね。: So it isn't purely the better option.
ja2en.早さを取るか、道しるべを取るか。普通に話せたなら、その中間だよ。: Speed, or a signpost. Speak with him normally and you land between the two.
ja2en.信頼は単純なボーナスではなく、探索の形を変える。: Trust isn't a simple bonus. It changes the shape of the search.
ja2en.その通り。まず、開始時に何を知っているか、どの部屋が開いているかを比べる。: Precisely. Compare what you know at the start, and which rooms are open to you.
ja2en.時計だけを見て、得した損したと決めない。: Don't judge gain and loss by the clock alone.
ja2en.情報があれば無駄足を減らせる。自由があれば、先に別の場所へ行ける。: Knowledge saves you wasted steps. Freedom lets you get somewhere else first.
ja2en.自分が迷いやすいなら、信頼が助けになる。: If I'm the sort to get lost, trust helps.
ja2en.地図を覚えているなら、早く動けることが助けになるかもしれない。: And if you have the map by heart, being able to move early may help more.
ja2en.零度警部に嫌われる攻略を勧めてません？: Are you recommending a walkthrough where Inspector Reido dislikes me?
ja2en.勧めてはいないよ。人間関係まで最短化すると、食事会で席がなくなる。: I recommend nothing. Optimise your relationships too far and you run out of seats at dinner.
ja2en.それは普通に困ります。: That would genuinely be a problem.
ja2en.ヒントではなく、舞黒さん自身の話を聞いてもいいですか？: Instead of a hint, may I hear about you for once?
ja2en.私の話かい。困ったな、嬉しいな。では茶を淹れよう。: About me? How awkward. How pleasant. Let me pour the tea.
ja2en.さっきから一杯も出てきていませんけど。: You haven't poured a single cup since I got here.
ja2en.死んでから一番不便なのは、茶を飲めないことではない。淹れられないことだよ。: The most inconvenient thing about being dead is not that I cannot drink tea. It is that I cannot make it.
ja2en.この館で一番好きな場所は？: What's your favourite place in this house?
ja2en.客のいる部屋だね。館は人を迎えて、ようやく館になる。: Whichever room has guests in it. A house only becomes a house once it receives people.
ja2en.資料室は好きだが、模型をあれほど大きくした覚えはないよ。: I am fond of the archive, but I do not recall making the model that large.
ja2en.館主公認ではなかった。: So it wasn't approved by the master of the house.
ja2en.次に建てる時は、もう少し小さくするよう言っておこう。: Next time I build one, I shall ask for something smaller.
ja2en.次がある言い方をしないでください。: Please don't talk as though there'll be a next time.
ja2en.舞黒さんは、客が帰った後は何をしていたんですか？: What did you do after the guests had gone home?
ja2en.昔なら片づけだね。今は片づけられないので、散らかったまま眺める。: Once, the tidying up. Now I cannot tidy anything, so I look at the mess instead.
ja2en.幽霊って、意外と手持ち無沙汰なんですね。: Ghosts are surprisingly at a loose end, aren't they.
ja2en.だから相談所はありがたい。君が来ると、館の時計が少し賑やかになる。: Which is why this room is a gift. When you come, the clocks of the house grow a little livelier.
ja2en.画面まで賑やかになりすぎる時がありますけど。: Sometimes the screen gets rather too lively as well.
ja2en.それは別の相談項目にしておいた。: I made that a separate item on the menu.
ja2en.館主が不具合を仕様にしました。: The master of the house has reclassified a bug as a feature.
ja2en.舞台袖の記録を読む: Read the notes from the wings
ja2en.これは館の設計図ではないね。『仕様書』と書いてある。: This is not the plan of the house. It says “specification.”
ja2en.館主が読んではいけない種類の資料です。: That is precisely the sort of document a house's master should not be reading.
ja2en.同じ一日を歩き直しても、違う発見になるよう順番を組んだらしい。: It seems the order was arranged so that walking the same day again yields different discoveries.
ja2en.いきなり核心に近い開発裏話を読むの、やめてもらえます？: Could you not read the behind-the-scenes notes that come this close to the heart of it?
ja2en.零度警部の信頼も、単純なご褒美にはしなかったそうだ。: Inspector Reido's trust, it says here, was not made into a simple reward either.
ja2en.信じられれば情報が増える。信じられなければ、先に動ける。: Trusted, and you learn more. Not trusted, and you can move sooner.
ja2en.人間関係をタイムアタックに使わないでください。: Please stop using human relationships for a time attack.
ja2en.失敗も後の会話へ持ち越す。探偵の見落としも、物語には立派な発見なのさ。: Failures are carried into later conversations too. A detective's oversight is, to a story, a fine discovery.
ja2en.少し綺麗にまとめて、誤魔化しましたね？: You wrapped that up rather neatly to change the subject, didn't you?
ja2en.この仕様書、選択に正解と不正解を付けないと書いてあります。: This specification says the choices are never marked right or wrong.
ja2en.その瞬間に気づいたことを、後の会話へ持ち越すためだそうだ。: So that whatever you noticed in that moment can be carried into the conversations after it.
ja2en.失敗も分岐の材料になる？: So failure is material for the branching too?
ja2en.正解するまで戻すと、探偵が迷った時間まで物語から消えてしまう。: Rewind until you get it right, and even the time the detective spent hesitating vanishes from the story.
ja2en.私の立ち尽くした時間まで保存されているんですね。: So even the time I stood there frozen has been kept.
ja2en.作者は探偵より執念深いらしい。: The author, it seems, is more tenacious than the detective.
ja2en.聞き捨てならない情報が出ました。: That is not a remark I can let pass.
ja2en.安心して。館主も勝手に黒塗りやドットにされる。: Don't worry. The master of the house gets blacked out and pixelated without being asked, too.
ja2en.開発資料への苦情窓口はどこです？: Where do I file a complaint about the development notes?
ja2en.受付担当が当事者なんですけど。: The complaints desk is staffed by the party responsible.
ja2en.画面が時々安定しないことについて: About the screen acting up now and then
ja2en.相談所の画面が時々、まったく違う姿になるんですけど。: Sometimes this room turns into something else entirely.
ja2en.館も長く生きると、たまには模様替えをしたくなる。: A house that lives long enough occasionally fancies redecorating.
ja2en.黒塗りやドット絵や配信になる模様替えがあります？: Is blacked out, pixel art, or a live stream really redecorating?
ja2en.流行に敏感な館だろう。: A house with an eye for fashion, wouldn't you say.
ja2en.幽霊がVTuberを始める流行は知りません。: I'm not aware of a fashion for ghosts becoming streamers.
ja2en.肉体がないという点では、適性が高いと思わないかい？: Having no body does rather suit the work, don't you think?
ja2en.そこだけ妙に説得力を出さないでください。: Please don't be oddly convincing about that one part.
ja2en.心配しなくても、話題を選ぶ画面は動かないよ。: Don't fret. The screen where you pick a topic never budges.
ja2en.会話を始めた後だけ不安定になる？: It only goes unstable after a conversation starts?
ja2en.そう。話を始める瞬間に、館がたまにくしゃみをする。: Just so. At the moment a talk begins, the house occasionally sneezes.
ja2en.くしゃみで解像度が落ちる館、初めて見ました。: A house that loses resolution when it sneezes. That's a first.
ja2en.どの姿になっても、相談の中身までは変わらない。: Whatever shape it takes, the substance of the consultation does not change.
ja2en.黒塗りになると怖さは三割増しです。: Blacked out, it's a good thirty percent more frightening.
ja2en.顔が見えないぶん、想像力で補えるだろう？: With the faces hidden, your imagination can make up the difference, can it not?
ja2en.配信ではコメント欄まで勝手に増えています。: In the stream, even the comments multiply on their own.
ja2en.館の壁まで視聴者として数えているからね。: I count the walls of the house among the viewers.
ja2en.不具合ではなく、低確率の余興として保存することにした。: Not a fault. I have decided to preserve it as a low-probability entertainment.
ja2en.言い方だけで修理を終えましたね。: You have completed the repair purely by rephrasing it.
ja2en.館主の権限は便利だろう？: The authority of the master of the house is a convenient thing.
ja2en.……舞黒さん。今日、輪郭しか見えないんですけど。: ...Mr Maicro. Today I can only see your outline.
ja2en.秘密を守る相談所らしいだろう？: Fitting, for a room that keeps secrets.
ja2en.相談員まで秘密にしないでください。: Please don't keep the counsellor a secret as well.
ja2en.なんか今日は、全体的にかくかくしていません？: Is everything a bit blocky today?
ja2en.ヒントはぼかすものだからね。解像度もぼかしてみた。: Hints are meant to be blurred. I blurred the resolution too.
ja2en.……どうして私が『ツッコミ担当』と表示されてるんですか？: ...Why am I being billed as “the straight man”?
ja2en.配信者がボケる以上、必要な役職だよ。: With the streamer playing the fool, it is a necessary post.
ja2en.まず配信者になった経緯を説明してください。: Start by explaining how you became a streamer.
ja2en.偶然だ。カメラも偶然、投げ銭ボタンも偶然だよ。: By chance. The camera was chance, and so was the donations button.
ja2en.ここへ来られたということは、一度は結末を見届けたんですよね。: If you're here, then you've seen an ending through at least once.
ja2en.たとえ苦い結末でも、ここでは失敗とは呼ばないよ。: Even a bitter ending is not called a failure in this room.
ja2en.では、何と呼ぶんです？: Then what do you call it?
ja2en.次へ持っていく質問票さ。反省文より、ずっと役に立つ。: A list of questions to carry forward. Far more use than a letter of apology.

ja2en.舞黒館を管理する女性46歳。半年前に夫が亡くなり、舞黒館を引き継ぐ。今回の宿泊イ: The woman who looks after Maicro House, aged 46. She took over the house when her husband died six months ago. She organised this overnight event.
ja2en.実の娘が行方不明で、生きていればメアリーや小出里亜くらいの年齢になるらしい。: Her own daughter is missing; were she alive, she would be about the same age as Mary or Koderia.
ja2en.料理、洗濯、掃除、家計簿管理まで何でもできるスペシャルなメイドさん。: A quite exceptional maid: cooking, laundry, cleaning, even the household accounts.
ja2en.熱いものに触れると咄嗟に指をなめる癖がある。: She has a habit of licking her fingers the instant she touches something hot.
ja2en.結婚して1年の夫婦の旦那でナイスガイの28歳。健康食品会社を起業し、順風満帆に事: A likeable twenty-eight-year-old, married a year. He founded a health food company and the business is sailing along. He is working on a new venture.
ja2en.妻の珠璃には頭が上がらない。休暇中でも仕事の連絡だけは手放せない性分らしい。: His wife Juri has the upper hand. Even on holiday, he seems unable to let go of work messages.
ja2en.結婚して1年の夫婦の美人妻の27歳。アパレルの個人ブランドを出しており、ヨーロッ: A beautiful twenty-seven-year-old, married a year. She runs her own clothing label, highly regarded in Europe in particular.
ja2en.SNSが好きでよく発信をしているらしい。: She loves social media and posts often.
ja2en.イギリスから来た24歳の女性。香水を作るのが趣味。: A twenty-four-year-old woman from England. She makes perfume as a hobby.
ja2en.宛名が不明の手紙で舞黒館に呼び出された。: She was summoned to Maicro House by a letter with no addressee.
ja2en.医学部の学生。21歳。冷静で落ち着いており、興味のあること以外には無頓着。: A medical student, twenty-one. Calm and composed, and indifferent to anything outside his interests.
ja2en.母親が亡くなったことがきっかけで医者を志す。: His mother's death is what set him on the path to medicine.
ja2en.横浜中央署で勤務をしている警部。冷静沈着で勘が鋭い。インテリ風に見えるが情に厚い: An inspector with the Yokohama Central police station. Cool-headed, with sharp instincts; he looks the intellectual but is warm-hearted. He came to Maicro House because he happened to be off duty. He cannot hold his drink; one cocktail is enough to put him in hospital.
ja2en.真歩流と愛理の父親。コンサルティング会社を経営しており、半年前から行方不明になっ: Father to Mahoru and Airi. He runs a consulting firm and has been missing for half a year.
ja2en.政治家かつ、戦争に反対していた資産家。1975年没。イギリスとフランスに留学をし: A politician and man of means who opposed the war. Died in 1975. He studied in England and France, learned Western culture there, and dreamed of drawing it into Japan to help his own culture grow. After returning he negotiated abroad as a politician, but the corruption of politics drove him out; he left office, took up commerce as a man of means, and worked to head off war with foreign dignitaries and to bind the nations closer. Because it was convenient for meeting friends from overseas, he built a Western house in Yamate, Yokohama, and lived there.

ja2en.三人の共通点: What the three have in common
ja2en.倒れた場所も行動も違う三人。まずは推測より先に、三人の身体に同じ痕跡が残っていな: Three people, each found in a different place, each doing something different. Before guessing, check whether the same trace is left on all three bodies.
ja2en.それぞれを同じ観点から調べれば、共通するものが見えてくるかもしれない。: Examine each of them from the same angle, and something they share may come into view.
ja2en.口にした場所へ戻る: Back to where it was drunk
ja2en.倒れた場所と、毒を口にした場所は同じとは限らない。二人の間をつなぐ、洗われずに残: Where someone collapsed is not necessarily where they swallowed the poison. Is there a vessel still unwashed that links the two of them?
ja2en.調理に使ったものだけでなく、キッチンの流しに置かれたままのものも確かめてみよう。: Check not only what was used for cooking, but whatever was left standing in the kitchen sink.
ja2en.液体が運ばれたなら、器だけでなく、途中でこぼれた場所にも痕跡が残る。昼の出来事を: If a liquid was carried, traces remain not only on the vessel but wherever it was spilled along the way. Think back over the afternoon.
ja2en.一階で飲み物がこぼれた場所を、もう一度調べてみよう。: Search again where a drink was spilled on the ground floor.
ja2en.毒の正体は確かめられたが、館に残った痕跡を見分ける知識がまだ足りない。実験は結果: The poison has been identified, but you still lack the knowledge to recognize its traces around the house. An experiment does not end with hearing the result.
ja2en.仮説を立てた人物へ結果を伝えれば、植物を調べる手がかりを借りられるかもしれない。: Take the result back to the person who proposed the theory, and you may borrow the knowledge to examine the plant.
ja2en.手元の本には、毒に使われた植物の性質が記されている。知識を得た今なら、以前は見分: The book in your hands describes the properties of the plant used for the poison. With that knowledge, you can now spot traces you could not before.
ja2en.一階の、植物が置かれた明るい部屋へ戻り、鉢を詳しく調べてみよう。: Go back to the bright room on the ground floor where the plant stands, and examine the pot closely.
ja2en.遺体のそばに残ったもの: What was left beside the body
ja2en.本人の身体だけでなく、身につけていたものにも毒が移っている可能性がある。小さな持: Poison may have transferred not only to the body but to what the victim was carrying. The smaller the belonging, the easier it is to miss.
ja2en.キッチンのご遺体を、所持品まで含めて確認してみよう。: Examine the body in the kitchen, belongings and all.
ja2en.毒を用意したなら、液体を扱った場所に痕跡が残る。きれいすぎる場所も、何もないとは: Whoever prepared the poison left traces where the liquid was handled. A place that is too clean is not necessarily an empty one.
ja2en.二階の個室で、天板だけ不自然に拭かれている机がないだろうか。: In the private rooms upstairs, is there a desk whose top alone has been unnaturally wiped?
ja2en.机から持ち出されたもの: What was taken from the desk
ja2en.拭かれた机で使われたものが、その後べつの場所へ運ばれた可能性がある。まず、その道: Whatever was used at that wiped desk may have been carried somewhere else afterwards. First, identify the implement.
ja2en.個室だけでなく、宿泊部屋の共用スペースに置き忘れられたものを確かめよう。: Check not only the private rooms but whatever was left behind in the shared space of the guest quarters.
ja2en.拭かれた道具が見つかった。その道具が昼間に触れた場所なら、消し切れなかった毒が移: You have found the wiped implement. If it touched something during the day, poison that could not be wiped away may have transferred there.
ja2en.二階の廊下で、昼にその道具を使って開けた仕掛けを調べてみよう。: Examine the mechanism in the second-floor corridor that you opened with it during the day.
ja2en.本に描かれた株: The plant drawn in the book
ja2en.館内に残った毒の痕跡は集まった。次は、手元の本に描かれた植物が、この館のどこかに: You have gathered every trace of poison inside the house. Next, find out whether the plant drawn in the book grows somewhere on the grounds.
ja2en.昼に歩いた庭へ戻り、ハーブが植えられていた一角を本の図と見比べてみよう。: Go back to the garden you walked through during the day and compare the herb bed with the illustration.
ja2en.庭の株を見つけただけでは、被害者から出た成分と同じものかは断定できない。比較する: Finding the plant in the garden is not proof that it matches what came out of the victims. To compare them, you need forensics.
ja2en.採取した株を、検査を手配できる人物へ見せてみよう。リビングにいる警察関係者なら頼: Show the plant you took to someone who can arrange a test. The police officer in the living room should be able to help.
ja2en.毒の正体は見えてきた。次は、調合された場所から被害者のもとまで、何を介して運ばれ: The poison itself is coming into focus. Now think about what carried it from where it was mixed to the victims.
ja2en.拭き取られた場所と、そこから持ち出されて別の場所でも使われた道具を、順番につない: Join up the place that was wiped clean and the implement taken from it and used elsewhere, in order.
ja2en.倒れた場所と口にした場所: Where they fell, where they drank
ja2en.三人が倒れた場所は一致しない。倒れた場所ではなく、それ以前に口にしたものへ視点を: The three did not fall in the same place. Look past where they fell, back to what they drank before it.
ja2en.お茶会で、誰の飲み物が誰へ渡ったのか。使われた器から確かめられないだろうか。: At the tea party, whose drink went to whom? Perhaps the vessels can tell you.
ja2en.セージに似た成分と、容器に残ったもの。この二つを組み合わせたとき何が起きるのか、: Something like sage, and something left in a container. What happens when those two are combined has not yet been tested.
ja2en.個人ではできない検査を、手配できる人物へ相談してみよう。: Take a test you cannot run yourself to someone who can arrange it.
ja2en.不自然に洗われた容器が見つかった。中身が消えていても、残った反応から用途を考えら: You have found a container washed unnaturally clean. Even with the contents gone, what remains may say what it was for.
ja2en.セージの性質について仮説を話した人物に、この容器を見せてみよう。: Show the container to the person who proposed the theory about sage.
ja2en.何かを混ぜて性質を変えたのなら、調合や持ち運びに使ったものが残るはずだ。: If something was mixed in to change its properties, whatever was used to mix and carry it should still exist.
ja2en.液体を入れられるもの、あるいは不自然に洗われているものが、誰かの荷物にないだろう: Is there something that could hold a liquid, or something washed unnaturally clean, in anyone's luggage?
ja2en.普通のセージは無害。それでも三人から似た成分が出たなら、品種か、加えられた何かに: Ordinary sage is harmless. If a similar compound came out of all three, then either the cultivar or something added to it is different.
ja2en.植物や薬の性質に詳しい人物なら、この矛盾から仮説を立てられないだろうか。: Someone who knows plants and drugs might build a theory out of that contradiction.
ja2en.手がかりは単独では答えにならない。新しく聞けるようになった話と、まだ説明できてい: No clue is an answer on its own. Tie the newly opened conversations to the traces you still cannot explain.

en2ja.And it's very good at staying silent. Tr: しかも黙秘が得意でね。事件の外に置かれたものを見直してごらん。
en2ja.If you want a different ending, doubt no: 別の結末を望むなら、最後の推理より、事件が起きる前の歩き方を疑うべきだ。
